steps.body: Skip-counting by ten jumps ten each time. Start at 23: 23, 33, 43, 53. The ones digit stays 3 — only the tens grow.
steps.narration: Skip-counting by ten jumps ten each time. Start at twenty-three: twenty-three, thirty-three, forty-three, fifty-three. The ones digit stays three — only the tens grow.

widget.prompt: Start at 23 and make 3 hops of 10. Tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: That hopped by ONES. Each hop is a whole ten: land on 53.

predict.prompt: You'll take 3 equal hops of 10, right from 23. How far from 23 will you end up in total?
predict.reveal: 3 equal hops of 10 cover 10 × 3 = 30 — repeated equal jumps ARE multiplication. Adding 10 + 3 = 13 mixes up the jump size with the number of jumps.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents skip ten.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for skip ten must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines skip ten.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: 37 + 10 = 47. Only the tens digit grows: 3 tens become 4 tens.
Add a ten to 37: the 7 stays, the tens go from 3 to 4, giving 47.

commonErrors.feedback: That added ONE. A ten-hop adds ten: 37 + 10 = 47.
That kept only the tens. Add ten to 37: the 7 stays, giving 47.

steps.body: You can start the tens-count anywhere. From 7: 7, 17, 27, 37, 47. Each jump is a ten.
steps.narration: You can start the tens-count anywhere. From seven: seven, seventeen, twenty-seven, thirty-seven, forty-seven. Each jump is a ten.

widget.prompt: Put this tens-count in order: it starts at 15 and jumps by ten.

misorderFeedback.feedback: Start at the smallest: 15 comes first, then add ten each time.

commonErrors.feedback: That added ONE. A ten-hop adds ten: 4 + 10 = 14.
That's 4 tens. One ten added to 4 is 14, not 40.

explanationVariants: When you count by tens, the ONES digit never changes — only the tens grow.
26, 36, 46 all end in 6: the ones digit holds while the tens climb.

options.label: the tens digit
options.feedback: The tens CHANGE (2, 3, 4, 5). It's the ones digit 6 that stays.

options.label: the ones digit (6)
options.feedback: Yes — the 6 holds; only the tens climb.

options.label: nothing stays
options.feedback: Look at the last digit — 6 every time. The ones digit stays.

hints: Look at the last digit each time.

widget.prompt: Start at 58, hop two tens. Where do you land?

commonErrors.feedback: That added just 2. Two TENS is 20 more: 58 + 20 = 78.

takeaways: The ones digit stays; the tens grow.
You can start from any number.
steps.teaser: next: counting a big pile as tens and ones.

concept.body: Slow down. 20, then a ten more is 30, then 40. Each jump adds a whole ten: 20, 30, 40, 50.
concept.narration: Slow down. Twenty, then a ten more is thirty, then forty. Each jump adds a whole ten: twenty, thirty, forty, fifty.

commonErrors.feedback: That added ONE. A ten-hop adds ten: 20 + 10 = 30.
That's the digits swapped. 20 and a ten more is 30.
